subject: Accounts
title: The Father of Accounting
text: In 1494, Luca Pacioli, an Italian mathematician, published 'Summa de arithmetica' in Venice – the first printed work on the double-entry system of book-keeping.
link: Double entry gives us the dual aspect concept: every debit has an equal credit. That is why your Trial Balance must agree and Assets always equal Liabilities + Capital.

subject: Law
title: One Act, three laws
text: The Indian Contract Act was enacted in 1872 with 266 sections. Its chapters on sale of goods and partnership were later taken out and made into separate laws – the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 and the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
link: That is why all three are read together. Sec 2(h) of the Contract Act defines a contract as 'an agreement enforceable by law', and the Sale of Goods Act uses the Contract Act's definitions wherever it has none of its own.
source: Wikipedia – Indian Contract Act, 1872; Sale of Goods Act, 1930

subject: Income Tax
title: From 1860 to 2025
text: India's first Income-tax Act was introduced in 1860 by James Wilson to refill the treasury after the 1857 crisis. It was followed by the Income-tax Act, 1961, which has now been replaced by the Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 1 April 2026.
link: Laws change, the logic stays: income is still computed head by head, deductions are allowed, and tax is charged on the total income. Master the structure and every new section becomes easy.
source: Wikipedia – Income tax in India; Income-tax Act, 2025

subject: GST
title: From VAT to GST
text: The value-added tax (VAT) was devised by Maurice Lauré of France – tried in 1954 in the Ivory Coast colony and adopted in France in 1958. Its idea: tax only the value added at each stage. India's GST follows the same idea and replaced State VAT, central excise, service tax and several other taxes.
link: This 'value added' idea is Input Tax Credit. Under Sec 16 of the CGST Act, a registered person sets off the tax paid on inputs against tax on output, so only the value added is taxed at each stage.
source: Wikipedia – Value-added tax; Goods and Services Tax (India)

subject: Accounts
title: 1 July – a day for three professions
text: 1 July is CA Day (ICAI was set up on 1 July 1949), GST Day (GST began on 1 July 2017) and National Doctors' Day (in memory of Dr B. C. Roy, born on 1 July 1882 and died on 1 July 1962). One date honours those who look after the nation's financial health and its physical health.
link: ICAI was created by the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 – the law that governs the profession you are preparing to join.
source: Wikipedia – ICAI; Goods and Services Tax (India); Bidhan Chandra Roy

subject: Law
title: The minor who changed contract law
text: In Mohori Bibee v Dharmodas Ghose (1903), a minor mortgaged his property to a moneylender. The Privy Council held that an agreement with a minor is totally void.
link: Sec 11 of the Contract Act: a person is competent to contract only if he has attained majority, is of sound mind and is not disqualified by law. A minor's agreement is therefore void ab initio – not merely voidable.
source: Wikipedia – Mohori Bibee v Dharmodas Ghose; Indian Contract Act, 1872

subject: GST
title: GST was born at midnight
text: GST was launched at a special midnight session (30 June – 1 July 2017) in the Central Hall of Parliament, after the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
link: The same amendment created the GST Council (Article 279A), which recommends GST rates and exemptions. In the CGST Act, Sec 9 is the charging section – the starting point for every GST computation.

subject: Accounts
title: AS and Ind AS – same numbers, same topics
text: Ind AS are named and numbered like the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). They became mandatory from 1 April 2016 for companies with a net worth of ₹500 crore or more.
link: In CA Inter you study AS; large and listed companies follow Ind AS. Many topics carry the same number in both – AS 2 and Ind AS 2 both deal with Inventories.

subject: Law
title: India's first-of-its-kind CSR law
text: The Companies Act, 2013 largely replaced the Companies Act, 1956. Its Section 135 made CSR spending mandatory for large companies – described as the only mandatory CSR law in the world.
link: Sec 135 applies when a company crosses any one threshold: net worth ₹500 crore, turnover ₹1,000 crore or net profit ₹5 crore. Such a company must spend at least 2% of its average net profit of the last three years on CSR.

subject: Accounts
title: Debit and Credit – the Latin roots
text: It is said that Pacioli's Summa used the Latin words 'debere' (to owe) and 'credere' (to entrust) for the two sides of a transaction – the roots of our words Debit and Credit.
link: Every journal entry you pass is that 500-year-old idea in action: one account receives (debit), another gives (credit), and the two are always equal.

subject: Auditing
title: Why is it called 'Audit'?
text: The word 'audit' comes from the Latin 'audire' – to hear. In early days accounts were read aloud and the auditor 'heard' them before approving.
link: Hearing is still evidence today: inquiry is one of the audit procedures under SA 500 (Audit Evidence) – but inquiry alone is not enough, it must be backed by other evidence.

subject: Costing
title: Where 'standard time' came from
text: Time and motion study combines Frederick Taylor's time study with Frank and Lillian Gilbreth's motion study (the family made famous by 'Cheaper by the Dozen').
link: Their work gave us the standard time for a job – the base for standard costing and the Labour Efficiency Variance you calculate in Cost & Management Accounting.

subject: Financial Management
title: The Rule of 72 is 500+ years old
text: Divide 72 by the interest rate to estimate how many years money takes to double. An early reference to this rule appears in Luca Pacioli's Summa of 1494 – the same book that gave us double entry.
link: At 12% p.a. money doubles in about 6 years (72 ÷ 12). This is the time value of money – the base of NPV and IRR in Capital Budgeting.

subject: Strategic Management
title: Five forces, one article
text: Michael Porter's Five Forces framework was first published in the Harvard Business Review in 1979 and is still the starting point for industry analysis.
link: In SM answers, analyse an industry through the five forces: rivalry among competitors, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of buyers and bargaining power of suppliers.

subject: Auditing
title: The scandal that changed audit law
text: After Enron's fraud came out in October 2001, its auditor Arthur Andersen – one of the world's five largest audit firms – collapsed. The USA then passed the Sarbanes–Oxley Act, 2002: it created the PCAOB to regulate auditors, stopped auditors from consulting for their audit clients (Sec 201), made the CEO and CFO certify financial reports (Sec 302) and required reporting on internal controls (Sec 404).
link: India has similar safeguards in the Companies Act, 2013: Sec 144 bars the auditor from services such as investment advisory, and Sec 143(3)(i) requires the auditor to report on internal financial controls.

subject: Costing
title: Overheads that follow activities
text: Robin Cooper and Robert Kaplan brought Activity-Based Costing into the spotlight in the 1980s, as firms found that one blanket overhead rate was distorting product costs.
link: ABC assigns overheads through cost drivers – for example, set-up cost on the number of set-ups – so each product bears the cost of the activities it actually uses.

subject: Financial Management
title: A Nobel Prize for capital structure
text: The Modigliani–Miller theorem on capital structure was first proposed in 1958. Franco Modigliani received the 1985 Nobel Prize in Economics for this and other work.
link: MM is one of the capital structure theories you study along with the Net Income and Net Operating Income approaches – learn the assumptions of each, as questions often test them.

subject: Strategic Management
title: Stars, cash cows and dogs
text: The BCG growth-share matrix was introduced in 1970 in the Boston Consulting Group essay 'The Product Portfolio'.
link: It classifies businesses by market growth and market share into Stars, Cash Cows, Question Marks and Dogs – cash from Cash Cows is used to build Question Marks into Stars.

subject: Auditing
title: Satyam – India's wake-up call
text: In 2009, Satyam's chairman B. Ramalinga Raju confessed that the company's accounts had been manipulated by about ₹7,000 crore.
link: Stronger checks followed in the Companies Act, 2013 – mandatory rotation of auditors (Sec 139(2)) and the National Financial Reporting Authority (Sec 132), set up in October 2018 to oversee audits of listed and large companies.
source: Wikipedia – Satyam scandal; National Financial Reporting Authority

subject: Strategic Management
title: Kodak invented the digital camera
text: Steven Sasson built the first self-contained digital camera at Kodak in 1975. It weighed about 3.6 kg and had just 0.01 megapixel.
link: A classic SM lesson: an internal strength (innovation) is wasted if strategy does not respond to changes in the external environment. Link it to SWOT and environmental scanning.

subject: Strategic Management
title: The Balanced Scorecard
text: Robert Kaplan and David Norton described the Balanced Scorecard in a 1992 article, so that firms would measure more than just profits.
link: It looks at performance from four perspectives – Financial, Customer, Internal Business Process, and Learning & Growth.
